root_cause: rich.cells measured width one codepoint at a time from a single CELL_WIDTHS table (rich/_cell_widths.py). Multi-codepoint graphemes were summed per codepoint: a ZWJ sequence like woman+ZWJ+wrench counted 4 cells instead of 2, and a narrow base followed by VS-16 (U+FE0F), e.g. '⬇️' or '♻️', counted 1 instead of 2 (issue #3897). chop_cells and set_cell_size also split between codepoints, so wrapping or cropping could cut a grapheme in half. Codepoints above the table's last range fell through to width 1.
best_solution: Replace the single width table with per-Unicode-version tables taken from wcwidth: package rich/_unicode_data holds VERSIONS (4.1.0 to 17.0.0), _parse_version (pads '1' or '1.2' to a 3-tuple and raises ValueError on bad input), and a cached load(version='auto') that reads the UNICODE_VERSION env var, maps 'latest' or invalid input to 17.0.0, and otherwise picks the nearest lower listed version via bisect (4.1.0 for anything below it). It returns a CellTable NamedTuple (unicode_version, widths, narrow_to_wide frozenset of VS-16-widened chars). In cells.py: get_character_cell_size(ch, unicode_version) returns 0 above the table's last range. _cell_len skips the codepoint after a ZWJ and adds +1 when VS-16 follows a char in narrow_to_wide. New split_graphemes(text) returns (list of CellSpan (start, end, cells), total width): a ZWJ extends the previous span by 2 codepoints, VS-16 extends it and may widen it, and other zero-width chars attach to the previous span. New split_text(text, cell_pos) walks the spans and, when the cut lands inside a 2-cell grapheme, returns (left + ' ', ' ' + right). set_cell_size crops via _split_text, and chop_cells builds lines from grapheme spans. Reasoning from the statement: 'split strings in to sequences that produce a single glyph', and 'used in a few low-level functions' means cell_len, set_cell_size, chop_cells and a new split function all have to become grapheme-aware. 'Same way as wcwidth' means ZWJ and VS-16 rules plus versioned width data.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py imports CellSpan, cell_len, chop_cells, get_character_cell_size, split_graphemes, split_text from rich.cells. It checks get_character_cell_size ('\0'->0, '\u200d'->0, 'a'->1, '💩'->2, chr(918000)->0). test_split_text runs 27 cases, e.g. split_text('💩',1)==(' ',' '), split_text(FM+'x',2)==(FM,'x'), split_text('x',-1)==('','x'). test_split_graphemes expects exact span lists and totals, e.g. 'a👩\u200d🔧b' -> [(0,1,1),(1,4,2),(4,5,1)], 4; '⬇️' -> [(0,2,2)], 2; '♻♻️' -> [(0,1,1),(1,3,2)], 3. tests/test_unicode_data.py imports VERSIONS, _parse_version, load from rich._unicode_data and requires load(v).unicode_version to map to exact version strings: '0'/'4.2.1'->'4.1.0', '5.0.1'->'5.0.0', '5.1.1'->'5.1.0', '18.0.0'->'17.0.0', and 'foo'/'a.b.c'/'1.2.3a'->'17.0.0'. Every version in VERSIONS must be loadable. tests/test_text.py: test_wrap_long_multi_codepoint (FM*5 wrapped at width 4 gives [FM*2, FM*2, FM+'  ']) and test_wrap_multi_codepoint (FM*6+' '+FM*4 at width 12 gives two lines).
locating_signals: The statement is the PR description: 'split strings in to sequences that produce a single glyph' and 'used in a few low-level functions' point to rich/cells.py (cell_len, get_character_cell_size, set_cell_size, chop_cells), and 'uses the data from wcwidth' points to replacing rich/_cell_widths.py. No function names appear in it. CellSpan, split_text, split_graphemes' (spans, total) return shape, the rich._unicode_data package, load/_parse_version/VERSIONS and the 4.1.0..17.0.0 version list exist only in the hidden tests. The linked issue #3897 (read by URL only) gives the VS-16 expectation cell_len('⬇️')==2.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs FAIL in the Kaggle env (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass false; patch_labels resolved=False for all). v4 (191s, 109 calls) added rich/_graphemes.py with a unicodedata-category iter_graphemes and only imported it into cells.py, never using it, so behavior was unchanged. v6 (73s) produced an empty patch. v7 deleted the closing docstring quote of cached_cell_len and called the undefined get_grapheme_cell_size/iter_graphemes. The file then fails to parse (SyntaxError: invalid character '。' from the __main__ demo text), which breaks every rich import. It also added a stray test_graphemes.py at the repo root. v8 (7406 chars) added rich/graphemes.py that yields grapheme strings (combining ranges + ZWJ) and made cell_len sum get_character_cell_size(ord(g[0])). It also wrote a junk duplicate file literally named 'rich/graphemes.py`'. It did not update chop_cells or set_cell_size, and it has no VS-16 widening, no CellSpan/split_text/split_graphemes span API and no rich._unicode_data. In every non-syntax-error run the failure is at collection time: ImportError 'cannot import name CellSpan from rich.cells' and ModuleNotFoundError 'rich._unicode_data'.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a PR description for a large feature ('adds the capability to split strings...'), the hidden tests almost always import new public names that the description never spells out. Read the linked issue, reuse the vocabulary the description does give ('split', 'graphemes', 'cell'), and put a public helper where existing tests import from (here rich.cells) rather than in a new private module. If a partial answer is all you can do, keep the change importable and minimal. Never ship a patch that breaks the module's syntax: run python -c 'import pkg.module' and the existing test file before finishing, because a SyntaxError or a dead import zeroes every test, including ones that passed before. Do not create stray files (repo-root tests, names with backticks).
